module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 568

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/568](https://www.erdosproblems.com/568)
- [EFRS93] Erdős, P. and Faudree, R. J. and Rousseau, C. C. and Schelp, R. H., Ramsey size linear
  graphs. Combin. Probab. Comput. (1993), 389-399.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos568

/--
Let $G$ be a graph such that $R(G,T_n)\ll n$ for any tree $T_n$ on $n$ vertices and
$R(G,K_n)\ll n^2$. Is it true that, for any $H$ with $m$ edges and no isolated vertices,
$$R(G,H)\ll m?$$

In other words, is $G$ Ramsey size linear?

This problem is #33 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_568 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      (∃ c₁ > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (n : ℕ) (T : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
        T.IsTree → (SimpleGraph.graphRamsey G T : ℝ) ≤ c₁ * n) →
      (∃ c₂ > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (n : ℕ),
        (SimpleGraph.graphRamsey G (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)) : ℝ) ≤ c₂ * (n : ℝ) ^ 2) →
      G.IsRamseySizeLinear := by
  sorry

end Erdos568

reformulations.difference: Each asymptotic bound '≪' of the source (R(G,T_n) ≪ n, R(G,K_n) ≪ n^2, R(G,H) ≪ m) is encoded as an explicit positive constant that must work for ALL n (all trees on Fin n, all K_n including n = 0, all H on Fin n with no isolated vertices), rather than only for sufficiently large n / sufficiently many edges. G is restricted to a vertex type in `Type`, and the trees and the graphs H to vertex types `Fin n`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Hypotheses: 'for all n' trivially implies 'eventually'. Conversely, only finitely many n lie below the threshold, and each has finitely many graphs on Fin n; the maximum Ramsey value over them can be absorbed into the constant, since the right-hand side is at least the constant for n ≥ 1. The n = 0 cases are harmless: no tree lives on Fin 0, and R(G,K_0) = 0. Conclusion: a graph H with no isolated vertices has at most 2m vertices (handshake lemma), so graphs with fewer than m₀ edges have fewer than 2m₀+1 vertices; there are finitely many of them, so their Ramsey values are bounded and can be absorbed, using m ≥ 1 when n ≥ 1. When n = 0, R = 0 ≤ c·0. Restricting to Fin n and Type 0 loses nothing, since graphRamsey is invariant under isomorphism. I proved in Lean (/workspace/review/equiv.lean, no sorry, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound) that the right-hand side of erdos_568 (checked: erdos_568 has type `True ↔ P568`, with `True` being the default display of `answer(sorry)`) is equivalent to the version where every bound is required only eventually or for H with at least m₀ edges.

review.notes: The statement agrees word for word with erdosproblems.com/568, and the UCSD collection's #33 poses the same question. `graphRamsey` and `IsRamseySizeLinear` match the standard definitions (non-induced copies; H ranges over graphs with no isolated vertices; bound c·e(H)). For finite graphs Ramsey's theorem makes the set in `graphRamsey` nonempty, so the `sInf ∅ = 0` default is never reached. Boundary cases checked in Lean: R(G, any graph on Fin 0) = 0; R(G, K_0) = 0; R(G, H) = 0 when G has an empty vertex type; no tree on Fin 0. All of these make the corresponding inequalities 0 ≤ 0 or vacuous. The hypotheses are satisfiable by nontrivial graphs (e.g. K_3), so the statement is not vacuous. The tree hypothesis is always satisfied: by Chvátal's theorem, R(G,T_n) ≤ R(K_p,T_n) = (p−1)(n−1)+1 ≤ p·n for G on p vertices. This redundancy is inherited from the source, not a formalization defect; both the source and the Lean effectively ask whether R(G,K_n)=O(n^2) implies G is Ramsey size linear. The 1993 EFRS paper's full text was not accessible (paywalled; the Rényi archive PDF link returns 404), so only its abstract was read; that abstract confirms the definition of Ramsey size linear. The status `research open` agrees with erdosproblems.com (OPEN) and the teorth database.
